title: Degree-zero restriction to a closed subset of a spectral space (sheaves of sets)
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subset such that for every $x\in X$ the intersection $Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (in particular nonempty). Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$ (a functor from the open subsets of $X$, ordered by inclusion, to sets, satisfying the gluing condition for every open covering), and let $\mathcal F|_Z$ be its inverse image along the inclusion $i:Z\to X$: the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $\theta:i_p\mathcal F\to\mathcal F|_Z$ of the presheaf $i_p\mathcal F:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq U}\mathcal F(V)$ on $Z$ ($V$ open in $X$, colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of sets over the directed set of such $V$ ordered by reverse inclusion, coprojections $\iota^U_V$), i.e. the construction of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then the restriction map $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$, $s\mapsto\theta_Z(\iota^Z_X(s))$ (the component at $X$ of the unit $\mathcal F\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)$), is bijective.

proof.text:
*Step 1 (restriction maps, stalks, injectivity).* For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $X$ and an open $W\subseteq X$ write $r_{\mathcal G,W}:\mathcal G(W)	o(\mathcal G|_Z)(W\cap Z)$, $s\mapsto	heta_{W\cap Z}(\iota^{W\cap Z}_W(s))$, so $r_{\mathcal G}=r_{\mathcal G,X}$ is the map of the statement; these maps commute with restrictions, and for a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal G	o\mathcal G'$ of sheaves of sets with induced $\varphi|_Z:\mathcal G|_Z	o\mathcal G'|_Z$ (sheafification of $i_p\varphi$) one has $(\varphi|_Z)_{W\cap Z}\circ r_{\mathcal G,W}=r_{\mathcal G',W}\circ\varphi_W$ (definitions of $i_p\varphi$ and of sheafification of a morphism, [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]). Stalks $\mathcal G_x=\varinjlim_{W
i x}\mathcal G(W)$ are directed colimits of sets, so $s_x=s'_x$ for $s,s'\in\mathcal G(W)$ iff $s|_{W'}=s'|_{W'}$ for some open $x\in W'\subseteq W$, and every element of $\mathcal G_x$ is a germ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-stalk] applied to $i:Z	o X$, for $z\in Z$ there is a bijection $c_{\mathcal G,z}:\mathcal G_z	o(\mathcal G|_Z)_z$ with $c_{\mathcal G,z}(s_z)=(r_{\mathcal G,W}(s))_z$ for $W
i z$ open, $s\in\mathcal G(W)$. It is natural: $(\varphi|_Z)_z(c_{\mathcal G,z}(s_z))=((\varphi|_Z)(r_{\mathcal G,W}s))_z=(r_{\mathcal G',W}(\varphi_Ws))_z=c_{\mathcal G',z}(\varphi_z(s_z))$. Two consequences. (*) If $\varphi$ is injective on sections over every open of $X$, then $\varphi|_Z$ is injective on sections over every open of $Z$: $\varphi_z$ is injective (if $\varphi(s)_z=\varphi(s')_z$ then $\varphi(s|_{W'})=\varphi(s'|_{W'})$ on some $W'
i z$, so $s|_{W'}=s'|_{W'}$), hence so is $(\varphi|_Z)_z=c_{\mathcal G',z}\varphi_zc_{\mathcal G,z}^{-1}$, and two sections of $\mathcal G|_Z$ with the same image then have equal germs at every point, so are equal [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs]. (**) Every $x\in X$ specializes to a point of $Z$: by hypothesis there is $z\in Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$, and every open $W
i z$ contains $x$ (otherwise $\overline{\{x\}}\subseteq X\setminus W$). Injectivity of $r_{\mathcal F}$: let $s,s'\in\mathcal F(X)$ with $r_{\mathcal F}(s)=r_{\mathcal F}(s')$, let $x\in X$ and $z$ as in (**). Then $c_{\mathcal F,z}(s_z)=(r_{\mathcal F}s)_z=(r_{\mathcal F}s')_z=c_{\mathcal F,z}(s'_z)$, so $s_z=s'_z$, i.e. $s|_W=s'|_W$ for an open $W
i z$; as $x\in W$, $s_x=s'_x$. Hence $s=s'$ [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs].

proof.text: *Step 2 (finite constant sheaves; Tag 0CAM).* Claim: if $X'$ is a spectral space, $Z''\subseteq X'$ closed with $Z''\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ connected for all $x\in X'$, and $S$ a finite set, then restriction $\rho:\mathrm{LC}(X',S)\to\mathrm{LC}(Z'',S)$ of locally constant maps is bijective. Injective: if $g,g'$ are locally constant and agree on $Z''$, the set $\{g=g'\}$ is open (both are constant near each point) and contains $Z''$; for $x\in X'$ it contains a $z\in Z''\cap\overline{\{x\}}$, hence $x$ (as in Step 1 (**)). Surjective, by induction on the number $m$ of values of $h\in\mathrm{LC}(Z'',S)$ ($m\le|S|$): if $m=0$ then $Z''=\emptyset$, hence $X'=\emptyset$ (each $Z''\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is nonempty) and there is nothing to do; if $m=1$, $h$ is constant with value $s$ and the constant map $s$ on $X'$ restricts to $h$. If $m\ge2$, pick a value $s$ and put $Z_1=h^{-1}(s)$, $Z_2=Z''\setminus Z_1$; both are closed in $Z''$ ($h$ is locally constant, so its fibres are open and closed) and $Z''=Z_1\amalg Z_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-closed-clopen-decomposition-lift] $X'=X_1\amalg X_2$ with $X_1,X_2$ closed, hence also open, and $Z_i=Z''\cap X_i$. $X_2$ is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-closed-subspace], $Z_2=Z''\cap X_2$ is closed in $X_2$, and for $x\in X_2$ the closure of $\{x\}$ in $X_2$ is $\overline{\{x\}}\subseteq X_2$, so $Z_2\cap\overline{\{x\}}=Z''\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (connectedness of a subset does not depend on the ambient space). $h|_{Z_2}$ takes $m-1$ values, so by induction it is the restriction of some $h_2\in\mathrm{LC}(X_2,S)$. The map equal to $s$ on $X_1$ and to $h_2$ on $X_2$ is locally constant ($X_1,X_2$ open) and restricts to $h$ on $Z''=Z_1\amalg Z_2$.

proof.text: *Step 3 (finite products of pushed-forward constant sheaves).* Let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n\subseteq X$ be closed ($n\ge0$), $S_1,\dots,S_n$ finite sets, $\mathcal G_k=(i_{Z_k})_*\underline{S_k}_{Z_k}$ ($\mathcal G_k(V)=\mathrm{LC}(V\cap Z_k,S_k)$) and $\mathcal P=\prod_k\mathcal G_k$, computed sectionwise with projections $p_k$. Claim: $r_{\mathcal P}$ is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] (b) the morphism $\mathcal P|_Z\to\prod_k\mathcal G_k|_Z$ with components $p_k|_Z$ is an isomorphism, so $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal P|_Z)\to\prod_k\Gamma(Z,\mathcal G_k|_Z)$, $t\mapsto((p_k|_Z)_Z(t))_k$, is bijective, and by naturality (Step 1) it sends $r_{\mathcal P}(s)$ to $(r_{\mathcal G_k}(p_{k,X}s))_k$; as $\mathcal P(X)=\prod_k\mathcal G_k(X)$, $r_{\mathcal P}$ is bijective if every $r_{\mathcal G_k}$ is. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-constant-restriction] (with $Z'=Z_k$, $S=S_k$) there is a bijection $\beta_k:\Gamma(Z,\mathcal G_k|_Z)\to\mathrm{LC}(Z\cap Z_k,S_k)$ with $\beta_k\circ r_{\mathcal G_k}=\rho_k$, the restriction $\mathrm{LC}(Z_k,S_k)\to\mathrm{LC}(Z\cap Z_k,S_k)$; so it suffices that $\rho_k$ is bijective. This is Step 2 for $X'=Z_k$, $Z''=Z\cap Z_k$: $Z_k$ is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-closed-subspace], $Z\cap Z_k$ is closed in $Z_k$, and for $x\in Z_k$ the closure of $\{x\}$ in $Z_k$ is $\overline{\{x\}}$ ($Z_k$ closed), so $(Z\cap Z_k)\cap\overline{\{x\}}=Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$, connected by hypothesis.

proof.text: *Step 4 (subsheaves).* Let $\mathcal F'$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$ with a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal P$, injective on sections over every open, into a sheaf $\mathcal P$ for which $r_{\mathcal P}$ is surjective. Claim: $r_{\mathcal F'}$ is surjective. Let $t\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F'|_Z)$ and choose $s\in\mathcal P(X)$ with $r_{\mathcal P}(s)=(\varphi|_Z)_Z(t)$. Let $x\in X$ and $z\in Z$ as in Step 1 (**). Write $c_{\mathcal F',z}^{-1}(t_z)=f_z$ with $f\in\mathcal F'(W)$, $W\ni z$ open (Step 1). Then $c_{\mathcal P,z}(\varphi_z(f_z))=(\varphi|_Z)_z(t_z)=((\varphi|_Z)_Zt)_z=(r_{\mathcal P}s)_z=c_{\mathcal P,z}(s_z)$, so $\varphi_z(f_z)=s_z$, i.e. $\varphi_{W'}(f|_{W'})=s|_{W'}$ for some open $z\in W'\subseteq W$, and $x\in W'$. Thus $X$ is covered by opens $W_x\ni x$ with $f^x\in\mathcal F'(W_x)$, $\varphi(f^x)=s|_{W_x}$. On $W_x\cap W_y$, $\varphi(f^x|)=s|=\varphi(f^y|)$, so $f^x|=f^y|$ by injectivity; by the sheaf property of $\mathcal F'$ they glue to $f\in\mathcal F'(X)$, and $\varphi_X(f)=s$ because both restrict to $s|_{W_x}$ on every $W_x$ ($\mathcal P$ is a sheaf). Then $(\varphi|_Z)_Z(r_{\mathcal F'}(f))=r_{\mathcal P}(\varphi_Xf)=r_{\mathcal P}(s)=(\varphi|_Z)_Z(t)$, and $(\varphi|_Z)_Z$ is injective by Step 1 (*), so $r_{\mathcal F'}(f)=t$.

proof.text: *Step 5 (general $\mathcal F$; conclusion).* By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-sheaf-colimit-constant-embeddings], $\mathcal F$ is the colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_\lambda)_\lambda)$, in sheaves of sets on $X$, of a directed system $(\mathcal F_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ such that each $\mathcal F_\lambda$ has a morphism, injective on sections, into a finite product $\mathcal P_\lambda=\prod_k(i_{Z_k})_*\underline{S_k}_{Z_k}$ with $Z_k$ closed and $S_k$ finite. By Step 3 $r_{\mathcal P_\lambda}$ is bijective, so by Step 4 every $r_{\mathcal F_\lambda}$ is surjective. Let $t\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] (a), $(\mathcal F|_Z,(c_\lambda|_Z)_\lambda)$ is a colimit of the directed system $(\mathcal F_\lambda|_Z)$ in sheaves of sets on $Z$. The space $Z$ is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-closed-subspace], so the open $U=Z$ satisfies the hypothesis of part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-directed-colimit-sections]: given an open covering of $Z$, each point lies in a quasi-compact open contained in a member (quasi-compact opens form a basis [def-weil-spectral-space]), finitely many of these cover the quasi-compact $Z$, and pairwise intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact ($Z$ is quasi-separated); the coverings of $Z$ by finitely many quasi-compact opens therefore form a cofinal system as required. Hence $t=(c_\lambda|_Z)_Z(t_\lambda)$ for some $\lambda$ and $t_\lambda\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F_\lambda|_Z)$. Choose $s_\lambda\in\mathcal F_\lambda(X)$ with $r_{\mathcal F_\lambda}(s_\lambda)=t_\lambda$; by naturality (Step 1) $r_{\mathcal F}(c_{\lambda,X}(s_\lambda))=(c_\lambda|_Z)_Z(r_{\mathcal F_\lambda}(s_\lambda))=t$. So $r_{\mathcal F}$ is surjective, and it is injective by Step 1: $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective.
